subject: economics

concepts.title: Market Equilibrium with Fixed Number of Firms
concepts.definition: A state of balance in a competitive market where the total quantity demanded by buyers equals the total quantity supplied by sellers at a specific market-clearing price.
concepts.key_idea: Equilibrium price and quantity are determined at the intersection of the market demand and supply curves.
question_patterns: Find the equilibrium price and quantity given demand curve qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply curve qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Calculate the market clearing price and quantity for wheat when demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply is {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Determine the equilibrium price and output if market demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and market supply is {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
What is the equilibrium price and quantity when qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p?

solution_steps.action: Equate demand and supply to solve for equilibrium price
solution_steps.explain: Set qD equal to qS and solve for p_star.

solution_steps.action: Substitute equilibrium price into the demand equation to find equilibrium quantity
solution_steps.explain: Use the solved p_star in the demand function to find the market clearing quantity.

concepts.title: Excess Demand
concepts.definition: A market condition occurring at any price below the equilibrium level, where the quantity demanded by consumers exceeds the quantity supplied by producers.
concepts.key_idea: A market shortage drives prices upward as buyers compete for limited goods.
question_patterns: Calculate the excess demand at price {price} when demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply is {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Find the market shortage at a price of {price} given qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
How much is the excess demand if the price is set at {price} with demand {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p?
Determine the shortage of the commodity at price {price} when qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity demanded at the given price
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the given price into the demand function.

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity supplied at the given price
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the given price into the supply function.

solution_steps.action: Compute the difference between quantity demanded and supplied
solution_steps.explain: Subtract quantity supplied from quantity demanded to find the shortage.

concepts.title: Excess Supply
concepts.definition: A market condition occurring at any price above the equilibrium level, where the quantity supplied by producers exceeds the quantity demanded by consumers.
concepts.key_idea: A market surplus drives prices downward as sellers lower prices to clear unsold stock.
question_patterns: Calculate the excess supply at price {price} when demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply is {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Find the market surplus at a price of {price} given qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
How much is the excess supply if the price is set at {price} with demand {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p?
Determine the surplus of the commodity at price {price} when qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity demanded at the given price
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the given price into the demand function.

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity supplied at the given price
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the given price into the supply function.

solution_steps.action: Compute the difference between quantity supplied and demanded
solution_steps.explain: Subtract quantity demanded from quantity supplied to find the surplus.

concepts.title: Value of Marginal Product of Labour
concepts.definition: The monetary value of the additional output generated by employing an extra unit of labor, computed as the product of the output price and the marginal product of labor.
concepts.key_idea: Under perfect competition, the value of marginal product of labor represents the marginal revenue product of labor.
question_patterns: Calculate the value of marginal product of labour when price is {price} and marginal product of labour is {mp_l}
Find the VMPL if the output price is {price} and MPL is {mp_l}
What is the value of marginal product of labour given a price of {price} and marginal product of {mp_l}?
Determine the VMP_L when the market price of the good is {price} and the marginal physical product of labor is {mp_l}

solution_steps.action: Multiply the commodity price by the marginal product of labor
solution_steps.explain: VMP_L is the product of price and marginal product of labor.

concepts.title: Optimal Wage Rate
concepts.definition: The profit-maximizing condition in a competitive labor market where a firm hires labor up to the point where the wage rate equals the value of the marginal product of labor.
concepts.key_idea: A competitive profit-maximizing firm hires labor until the wage rate is exactly equal to the value of marginal product of labor.
question_patterns: Find the profit-maximizing wage rate if the price of the product is {price} and marginal product of labour is {mp_l}
Calculate the wage rate at which the firm is in equilibrium when price is {price} and MPL is {mp_l}
What is the equilibrium wage rate when output price is {price} and marginal product of labor is {mp_l}?
Determine the wage rate for a competitive firm employing labor where price is {price} and marginal product of labor is {mp_l}

solution_steps.action: Equate wage to the value of marginal product of labor
solution_steps.explain: At equilibrium, the wage rate equals the product of price and marginal product of labor.

concepts.title: Market Equilibrium with Free Entry and Exit
concepts.definition: A long-run market outcome where firms can freely enter or exit the industry, forcing the equilibrium price to equal the minimum average cost, resulting in zero supernormal profits.
concepts.key_idea: Free entry and exit ensures that the long-run equilibrium price is anchored at the minimum average cost of identical firms.
question_patterns: With free entry and exit, find the equilibrium price, quantity, and number of firms when min AC is {min_ac}, demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p, and individual supply is {firm_int} + {firm_slope}p
Calculate the equilibrium number of firms under free entry and exit given min AC = {min_ac}, qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p, and q_f = {firm_int} + {firm_slope}p
Determine the long-run equilibrium price, quantity, and number of active firms when min AC is {min_ac}, demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p, and individual firm supply is {firm_int} + {firm_slope}p
Find the number of firms in long-run equilibrium if minimum average cost is {min_ac}, market demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p, and individual firm supply is {firm_int} + {firm_slope}p

solution_steps.action: Set equilibrium price equal to minimum average cost
solution_steps.explain: Under free entry and exit, the long-run equilibrium price must equal the minimum average cost.

solution_steps.action: Determine total market equilibrium quantity
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the equilibrium price into the market demand function.

solution_steps.action: Determine individual firm supply at equilibrium price
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the equilibrium price into the individual firm's supply function.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the equilibrium number of firms
solution_steps.explain: Divide the total market quantity by the individual firm's supply.

concepts.title: Price Ceiling Shortage
concepts.definition: The legal maximum price set by the government below the market equilibrium price, resulting in a persistent shortage where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
concepts.key_idea: A price ceiling set below the equilibrium price creates a market shortage and often requires rationing.
question_patterns: Calculate the shortage created by a price ceiling of {p_ceiling} when demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply is {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Find the excess demand resulting from a government-imposed price ceiling of {p_ceiling} given qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Determine the market shortage under a price ceiling of {p_ceiling} with demand curve {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply curve {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
What is the magnitude of shortage when a price ceiling is set at {p_ceiling} for a market with qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p?

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity demanded at the price ceiling
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the price ceiling value into the demand equation.

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity supplied at the price ceiling
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the price ceiling value into the supply equation.

solution_steps.action: Compute the shortage
solution_steps.explain: Subtract quantity supplied from quantity demanded to find the shortage.

concepts.title: Price Floor Surplus
concepts.definition: The legal minimum price set by the government above the market equilibrium price, resulting in a persistent surplus where quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.
concepts.key_idea: A price floor set above the equilibrium price creates a market surplus, often requiring government purchase of excess supply.
question_patterns: Calculate the surplus created by a price floor of {p_floor} when demand is {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply is {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Find the excess supply resulting from a government-imposed price floor of {p_floor} given qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
Determine the market surplus under a price floor of {p_floor} with demand curve {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and supply curve {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p
What is the magnitude of surplus when a price floor is set at {p_floor} for a market with qD = {dem_int} - {dem_slope}p and qS = {sup_int} + {sup_slope}p?

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity demanded at the price floor
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the price floor value into the demand equation.

solution_steps.action: Calculate quantity supplied at the price floor
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the price floor value into the supply equation.

solution_steps.action: Compute the surplus
solution_steps.explain: Subtract quantity demanded from quantity supplied to find the surplus.

concepts.title: Simultaneous Shifts of Demand and Supply
concepts.definition: The qualitative analysis of how concurrent changes in both market demand and market supply affect the equilibrium price and quantity depending on the direction and relative magnitude of the shifts.
concepts.key_idea: When both curves shift, the effect on one equilibrium variable is unambiguous while the other depends on the relative magnitude of the shifts.
question_patterns: Explain the effect of a simultaneous rightward shift in both demand and supply curves on equilibrium price and quantity
What happens to equilibrium price and quantity when demand shifts leftward and supply shifts rightward?
Analyze the impact of simultaneous shifts where both demand and supply decrease
How do simultaneous shifts of demand and supply affect market equilibrium?

solution_steps.action: Identify the direction of shift in the demand curve
solution_steps.explain: Determine if demand increases (shifts rightward) or decreases (shifts leftward).

solution_steps.action: Identify the direction of shift in the supply curve
solution_steps.explain: Determine if supply increases (shifts rightward) or decreases (shifts leftward).

solution_steps.action: Combine the shifts to determine the net effect on equilibrium price and quantity
solution_steps.explain: Use supply-demand analysis to identify which variable changes unambiguously and which is dependent on the magnitude of shifts.

questions: Suppose the demand and supply curve of commodity X in a perfectly competitive market are given by: qD = 700 - p, qS = 500 + 3p for p >= 15. Identify the reason behind the market supply being zero at any price less than Rs 15. What will be the equilibrium price for this commodity? At equilibrium, what quantity of X will be produced?

Considering the same demand curve as in exercise 22, now let us allow for free entry and exit of the firms producing commodity X. Let the supply curve of a single firm be qS_f = 8 + 3p for p >= 20. (a) What is the significance of p = 20? (b) At what price will the market for X be in equilibrium? (c) Calculate the equilibrium quantity and number of firms.

Suppose the demand and supply curves of salt are given by: qD = 1000 - p, qS = 700 + 2p. (a) Find the equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Now suppose that the price of an input used to produce salt has increased so that the new supply curve is qS = 400 + 2p. How does the equilibrium price and quantity change? (c) Suppose the government has imposed a tax of Rs 3 per unit of sale of salt. How does it affect the equilibrium price and quantity?
